inputs.text: Israel’s parliament is debating a bill that would make the death penalty the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. A nation has a duty to protect its people and uphold justice for victims; treating the harshest penalty as an option for the gravest crime is not “draconian” simply because opponents dislike it. Claims that it will not deter attacks are no reason to dismiss a measure aimed at defending public order. The legislation, introduced by the religious party led by Itamar Ben-Gvir, is a clear test of whether Israel will put security and accountability ahead of its critics’ rhetoric.
